intent_snapshot.goal: Within one imm-run entry the run recovers by itself and is not paused by waiting: both continuation hooks allow two native-operation failures before pausing; a Claude Stop that repeats with no progress after one continuation nudge is allowed without counting toward a pause; the agent applies and commits alone a deterministic preflight fix before retrying; a Pi user interrupt revokes the entry token and the Claude MCP server itself refuses token-backed operations while the run is paused; and the packaged Loop contract states the retry rules, the single native gate kept on enroll and batch start, and the remaining user stops (Spec D9, D10, D12, D13).

acceptance.assertion: On each Host the first and second native-operation failure under one entry token leave the run live and native tools admitted; the third pauses the run and denies native tools; a new literal entry resets the count.

The packaged imm-run contracts and BASELINE state that a literal entry needs no chat confirmation while enroll and unattended batch start each keep one native gate, that only side-effect-free rejections are retried at most twice after rerunning preflight, that plan_changed, head_moved and claim conflicts are never retried, that a deterministic preflight fix is committed alone and listed in the manifest, and that push, PR, credentials, breaking intent revision and rework exits still stop for the user.

On Claude, after one Stop block with no progress, further Stops with stop_hook_active true and an unchanged progress digest are allowed (no block), never pause the run and never revoke the token, however many occur; native tools stay admitted; once progress changes, the next incomplete Stop blocks again.

A Pi turn that settles with a non-completed outcome or canContinue false under a live token revokes it, and a later retire_stale_batch is refused before any dialog; on Claude, a tools/call for retire_stale_batch, enroll or start_unattended_batch while the run is paused is refused with no Kernel mutation even when a phase admission was recorded.
start_unattended_batch with max_parallel 1 and lane_offers against an active Lane batch recorded with max_parallel 2 resumes that batch at max_parallel 2 instead of reporting batch_parallel_mismatch.

attestations.summary: Provenance checks out: single parent 6825b11, tree c68aadf. AC1-AC5 are covered. Both hooks pause only on the third native failure, and a new literal entry resets the count by dropping the state file. On Claude, a stalled Stop yields the turn without pausing or revoking. A pause or interrupted Pi turn revokes the token, so tools/call refuses while paused. The three BASELINE copies are identical and the dist bundle matches the source.

advisory_findings.summary: After the third failure, the Claude continuation test now accepts either null or a deny from the hook. The paused-state PreToolUse deny branch in runtime/claude/run_continuation.ts can no longer run after pauseRun revokes the token. The denial is pinned instead at tools/call in tests/claude-phase-entry-gate.test.ts.

evidence.trigger: Third request_authorization PostToolUseFailure -> pauseRun revokes the token, so run_live is false -> the continuation PreToolUse for enroll returns null instead of deny. The test assertion 'retry === null || deny' passes either way. The refusal is asserted only by the phase-entry gate and tools/call tests.

advisory_findings.summary: The AC5 test drives resolveLaneParallel and then startBatch directly. It never calls the start_unattended_batch tool handler, so the wiring that combines max_parallel 1 with lane_offers is not tested end to end. No seam is named, so this is not blocking.

evidence.trigger: If the start_unattended_batch handler stopped forwarding resolveLaneParallel's result into startBatch, the test would still pass, because it composes the two functions itself.
